title: Mom lost both her son and her mental health
article: They shared a deadly "Folie à Deux," a rare psychotic disorder that afflicted mother and child and ended with the violent son being killed by police and his delusional mother found not criminally responsible for conspiring to kill their Mississauga neighbour.
Maybe now she will finally get the help she so badly needs.

Boketsu Boekwa, 52, "was and continues to suffer from a psychotic disorder, most likely schizophrenia," said Justice Michal Fairburn in finding her NCR. And that illness, likely shared by her 22-year-old son Marc Ekamba-Boekwa, set off a series of events that led to his death on March 20, 2015.

"The conduct was extremely serious, dangerous, and had tragic and profound consequences, including to members of the public and law enforcement officers upon whom we rely to keep us safe," wrote Fairburn in her decision released May 9.

According to a psychiatric assessment by a medical team at Ontario Shores, Boekwa began suffering from delusions as far back as 2010 when she quit work, sold her car and took her daughter out of school.

"It is also apparent that her son was similarly afflicted," noted the report. "Together they reinforced each other's delusional preoccupations. This rare condition is known as a shared psychotic disorder or Folie à Deux."

Boekwa came to believe neighbour Diana Cittadino was a witch. She believed her son was a king. And, along with the Illuminati, she believed Cittadino had played a role in stealing her son's throne and giving it to Queen Elizabeth. Cittadino had to die and they plotted to kill her together.
On that fateful day, Boekwa threw a knife at her neighbour and threatened to "bathe her family in blood."
Cittadino called police. When three officers arrived at the Boekwas' Mississauga townhouse, the mom came out swinging, striking one with a metal pot.
"She came to her front door to see her son, whom she believed to be a King, being arrested and she reacted aggressively as a result," according to the report.

As police tried to arrest her, her son came running at them with a knife. After two officers were stabbed, they all opened fire. Of their 19 gunshots, 11 hit Ekamba-Boekwa and one struck neighbour Suzan Zreik in the spine. The SIU cleared police of any wrongdoing.

In January, Fairburn ordered the psychiatric assessment after finding Boekwa guilty of conspiracy to commit murder; three counts of assault with a weapon; and uttering a death threat. In agreeing with the report's conclusion that the mom was incapable of knowing her actions were morally wrong, it's now up to the Ontario Review Board to determine if and when Boekwa may ever be released from a psychiatric hospital.
The judge ended her judgment with remarkably kind words to a woman who's lost both her son and her mental health.

"To Madame Boekwa, your daughter reports that, before events started to take shape, you were a positive, loving person who did not have problems with anyone. It is clear that you have a loving daughter who you love very much. This relationship will no doubt assist you as you move forward from this courtroom."
